To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

customer satisfaction is higher if service recovery truly makes up for what customers lost, if service recovery is perceived to be appropriate, and if service recovery efforts are perceived to be effective.

the effect of service recovery efforts on customer satisfaction is greater for outcome-related failure than for process-related failure, and that service recovery efforts that make up for what the customer has lost have a stronger effect than efforts that do not make up for what has been lost.

customer satisfaction is greatest when the type of service recovery matches the type of service failure, when the magnitude of the service failure is considered, and that prior experience with a service failure affects the effectiveness of service recoveries.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of the interaction between service failure and recovery efforts on customer satisfaction.
the development of a theoretical model that explains how service failure and recovery affect customer satisfaction.
the development of a theory-driven model that can be used to understand the impact of service failures on service recovery and customer satisfaction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
service failure and service recoveries should be considered as a single process.

customers are more satisfied when they receive service recovery efforts that are appropriate to the service failure they have experienced, and that this satisfaction is greater for customers with prior service failure experience.
service recovery efforts are more effective if they make up for what the customer has lost.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
service recovery efforts are more effective when they are tailored to the specific type of service failure and when they are perceived as a fair exchange for the service failure.
the effectiveness of service recoveries depends on the types of service failure and service failures.
service failure and service recoveries should be treated as a whole.
The main takeaway from our work is that
customers' mental accounting processes can be influenced by service failure and service failure recovery efforts.
service providers should be aware of the importance of matching service failure types and magnitude to service recovery types and efforts.
